source.acquisitionMethod: Controlled black-box observation of two lawfully installed external Barrier programs on an isolated peer loopback, executed by the capture producer under Tests/SystemTests/Plans/M1-024-barrier-client-handshake-fixtures.md and bounded to one connection window. Direction labelling is capture provenance rather than analysis: the capture producer supplied the server test port of the endpoint role it operated, and the sanitizer applied that producer-selected server-port role to label every retained run. No direction label is derived from payload content.

transport.networkScope: The recorder ran on the peer loopback interface and observed the Barrier leg there only; every retained byte comes from that peer-loopback observation. The wider transport leg that reached that host was an encrypted local forward whose contents the recorder did not capture, so no cleartext Barrier payload was observed or retained outside the peer-loopback leg and nothing is claimed about that encrypted leg. No identifying address, port or host name was recorded.

provenance.lawfulUseStatement: Both endpoints were lawfully installed external Barrier programs operated by their owner on hosts under that owner's control, and only externally observable application payload bytes were recorded. No Barrier or Deskflow source, header, constant table, generated implementation artifact or decompiled material was read, copied, linked or bundled.

sanitization.procedure: Allowlist sanitization by the capture producer's private temporary sanitizer, SHA-256 d273a45575b75d433e07fb29fe6361aa9d76bf62a9585645affc19698be004a4, whose self-test SHA-256 d8c5c6db42f0e2eac39946ded502e83795b70f7b0a2a8771da57db782b5f8794 passed 21 checks. The retained document keeps sequence numbers, direction labels and base64 application payload runs only; every packet header, address, port, timestamp and transport metadata key is dropped, and a private denylist scan over the decoded payload reported zero hits. Before the raw capture was deleted the independent reviewer re-ran that sanitizer over it and reproduced the retained document byte for byte.

behaviors: Seven contiguous application-payload runs numbered 1 through 7 were retained from a single bounded 9-second connection window.
Both direction labels occur and the retained labels alternate strictly, beginning with the run labelled server-to-client.
The retained runs decode to 15, 28, 8, 22, 36, 16 and 8 bytes in sequence order, totalling 133 bytes.
No input, clipboard or screen-switch traffic was observed inside the bounded window.

wireClaims.assertion: In this single observation the retained document holds exactly 7 application-payload runs whose decoded lengths are, in sequence order, 15, 28, 8, 22, 36, 16 and 8 bytes, totalling 133 bytes. The claim covers the retained bytes and their lengths only and asserts no field, message or framing meaning for any of them.

The 7 retained runs form a contiguous 1-based sequence in the order the recorder observed them inside the bounded window, and both direction labels occur. Ordering is an observation of the capture; it is not evidence of a message boundary, a request-response pairing or a protocol state machine.

Every retained direction label was assigned from the capture producer's selected server test port, which is recorded as capture provenance, and no label was derived from payload content. The independent reviewer confirmed that the opposite server-port selection yields a structurally valid document of the same run count and the same aggregate length with all 7 labels inverted, so only the producer-recorded role reproduces the registered digest.

limitations: One observation of one external version pair on one locked host pair; it represents nothing beyond that observation.

The observation ran with encryption disabled so that application payload bytes were observable. No payload under TLS was observed, and the MacKVM production TLS default stays enabled, fail-closed and unvalidated by this entry.

The recorder observed only the peer-loopback Barrier leg. The encrypted local forward that reached that host was not captured, so nothing about that leg, its transport or its endpoints is observed or claimed here.
The window is bounded to the connection handshake; no input, clipboard or screen-switch traffic exists in the retained fixture.
The external programs reported protocol version 1.6 through their own command-line metadata. That is a report by the external binaries and establishes nothing about on-wire version negotiation.

peer.os.build records not-reported because the capture producer did not record a Linux peer OS build identifier before the observation and MacKVM_Implementation_Package_v2/toolchain.lock.json pins the peer OS by name and version only. The value is recorded as unreported rather than inferred.
Windows was not executed in M1 under docs/adr/M1-SCOPE-001-linux-only-validation.md; this entry claims no Windows result and no Windows Barrier Server compatibility.

The private raw capture, the peer configuration and the private capture logs were deleted by the capture producer after M1-024 merged. They are not retained, must not be required or recreated, and re-deriving this fixture from raw bytes is therefore no longer repeatable.

The pre-deletion independent re-derivation of this fixture from the raw capture, together with the independent provenance, licensing, privacy and content review, is recorded in evidence/issues/M1-024/independent-review.md, which is the verification record of record for this entry.
Direction labels rest on the capture producer's selected server test port rather than on anything inside an observation, so a consumer that relies on direction relies on capture provenance.

sanitization.procedure: No new sanitization was needed because this entry introduces no new byte. The derived artifact records candidate frame offsets, lengths, candidate length-prefix values, the 7 marker bytes and the 4 bytes after them only; it copies no other payload byte and no payload text, and the deriving test rejects any printable payload text other than the marker in the artifact or in this entry.

behaviors: The 7 retained runs of BARRIER-EVID-0001 were re-read from the registered fixture without any new capture, and their 133 decoded bytes partition into 11 candidate frames under a candidate 4-byte unsigned big-endian length-prefix interpretation. A narrower 2-byte big-endian reading also partitions every run, so the prefix width is not uniquely established.
Under the candidate interpretation runs 5 and 6 each carry several complete candidate frames, 4 and 2, and no candidate frame spans two retained runs.
Two candidate frames, one under each direction label, begin with the same 7 marker bytes followed by the same 4 version bytes.
Every other payload byte is left uninterpreted and is recorded by offset and length only.

wireClaims.assertion: In this single observation a candidate framing interpretation, in which consecutive candidate frames each begin with a 4-byte unsigned big-endian length prefix whose value equals the number of bytes that follow it in that frame, partitions every one of the 7 retained runs exactly with zero remaining bytes. Under it the 7 runs hold 11 candidate frames, 1, 1, 1, 1, 4, 2 and 1 in sequence order, whose length values are 11, 24, 4, 18, 4, 4, 8, 4, 4, 4 and 4 and cover all 133 retained bytes. Reading the same first 4 bytes of each run as little-endian partitions none of the 7 runs. A narrower 2-byte big-endian reading also partitions all 7 runs, so this claim does not establish the prefix width and prefix width uniqueness stays unknown.

In this observation the first frame of run 1, labelled server-to-client, and the first frame of run 2, labelled client-to-server, each carry at run offset 4 the same 7 bytes 42 61 72 72 69 65 72, the ASCII spelling of the word Barrier, at the start of the frame payload. No other frame begins with those bytes. The claim states byte values and offsets only and assigns no message name or meaning to either frame.

In both marker-bearing frames the 4 bytes immediately after the marker, at run offsets 11 to 14, are 00 01 00 06. Read as two consecutive unsigned 16-bit big-endian integers they are 1 and 6, which coincides with the protocol version 1.6 that both external programs reported through their own command-line metadata. That coincidence is the only link between these bytes and a version; their width and meaning are left to M1-025, and no negotiation or other version is observed.

limitations: One observation of one external version pair on one locked host pair, re-read without any new capture; it represents nothing beyond that observation.

All 11 candidate length values lie between 4 and 24, so the three high-order bytes of every candidate prefix are zero. These bytes therefore do not uniquely establish a 4-byte prefix width, because a narrower 2-byte big-endian prefix also partitions all 7 runs, and they exercise no length value of 256 or more, no sign bit and no maximum frame length.

Under the candidate interpretation every retained run starts and ends on a candidate frame boundary. Runs 5 and 6 each carry several complete candidate frames, 4 and 2, so multiple complete candidate frames coalesced in a single retained run were observed. No candidate frame spans two retained runs, so fragmentation or split delivery was not observed.
A retained run is a direction run of the captured TCP byte stream. Its boundaries are capture and read boundaries, not protocol frame boundaries in general.
Only the marker bytes and the 4 bytes after them are identified inside any frame payload; every other payload byte stays uninterpreted.
The link between the 4 bytes after the marker and protocol version 1.6 rests only on the version the external programs reported through their own command-line metadata.

The observation ran with encryption disabled so that application payload bytes were observable. No payload under TLS was observed, and the MacKVM production TLS default stays enabled, fail-closed and unvalidated by this entry.
Windows was not executed in M1 under docs/adr/M1-SCOPE-001-linux-only-validation.md; this entry claims no Windows result and no Windows Barrier Server compatibility.
The private raw capture was deleted after M1-024 merged. This entry needs no raw byte because it re-reads only the registered sanitized fixture, whose SHA-256 and byte length it pins.
BARRIER-EVID-0001 is not rewritten, upgraded or superseded by this entry; its unknown fields stay unknown in that entry, and this entry records its own claims and unknowns.

No field offset, width, order or meaning is identified inside any frame payload beyond the marker bytes and the 4 bytes after them.

Every candidate length value is below 256 and a narrower 2-byte big-endian reading also partitions all 7 runs, so these bytes do not decide between a 4-byte prefix and a narrower big-endian prefix preceded by zero bytes. The exact prefix width is unknown, and M1-025 must not freeze an exact prefix width from this entry until separately approved discriminating evidence exists.

Whether the 4 bytes after the marker hold one value or two, and what they mean, is not established by these bytes alone.

source.acquisitionMethod: M1-WIRE-002 GitHub Issue #279 attempt 8: controlled black-box observation of two lawfully installed external Barrier 2.4.0 programs over a Linux loopback capture leg inside an SSH-forwarded disposable topology. The trigger was a deterministic synthetic non-personal long client screen name supplied through normal configuration and command-line inputs. The accepted runtime observation was an explicit protocol-error close under the pre-approved section-17 gate, not successful interoperability. No Barrier or Deskflow source, source-derived writeup, decompiled output, instrumentation, packet injection, patched binary or generated protocol byte sequence was used. Peer runtime logs and raw-pcap current availability are recorded with limitations because the attempt-8 remote temporary directory was unavailable when rechecked; no raw peer-log hash or raw-pcap-to-sanitized re-derivation is claimed in the repository.

transport.networkScope: The recorder observed only the Linux loopback leg between the external Barrier client and the SSH remote-forward listener. Inter-host traffic stayed inside SSH. Real addresses, ports, host names and user names are not recorded. The raw pcap stayed on role-capture and is not committed.

provenance.lawfulUseStatement: Both endpoints were lawfully installed external Barrier programs operated by their owner on hosts under that owner control. Only externally observable runtime behavior and sanitized prefix-position bytes are retained.
provenance.permittedUse: Input to M1-025 for freezing the exact Barrier top-level length-prefix width inside the MacKVM Barrier Protocol Adapter only. It does not authorize claims about message codes, field layout beyond the prefix, version negotiation, chunking, Windows behavior or production TLS behavior.
provenance.producer: M1-WIRE-002 attempt 8 capture producer, recorded in evidence/issues/M1-WIRE-002/attempt8/manual.md and metadata.json

reviewer.identity: Claude Opus 5.5 independent reviewer (Claude Code session), not the M1-WIRE-002 attempt-8 producer; second-pass review recorded in evidence/issues/M1-WIRE-002/independent-review.md Checkpoint 4

sanitization.procedure: Allowlist sanitization by Tools/Evidence/m1_wire_002_stream_analysis.py version 1. It reconstructs complete FIN-bounded TCP streams, evaluates width-4 and width-2 walks on identical bytes, and retains only bytes read as length-prefix positions by either walk; every other byte is replaced by a fill byte. The committed fixture contains no raw packet headers, real addresses, ports, host names, user names, generated screen-name content or payload text.

behaviors: One complete FIN-bounded connection was retained from the Linux loopback capture leg.
The client-to-server stream is 70019 bytes and partitions as one width-4 frame with payload length 70015.
The server-to-client stream is 23 bytes and partitions under both readings; discrimination occurs on the client-to-server stream.
Width 4 succeeds on every retained complete stream; width 2 fails on the client-to-server stream at offset 57514 with overrun declared 24929 and available 12503.

wireClaims.assertion: The retained complete streams establish a 4-byte unsigned big-endian top-level Barrier length prefix whose value is the number of payload bytes after the prefix for this observed external Barrier 2.4.0 behavior. Width 4 partitions every retained complete stream; the narrower 2-byte big-endian reading fails on the same bytes at offset 57514 with overrun declared 24929 and available 12503.

limitations: The runtime observation is an explicit protocol-error close, not successful interoperability.
Only the top-level length-prefix width, byte order and payload-length meaning are established.

No message codes, field layout beyond the prefix, maximum accepted length, chunking behavior, version negotiation, cross-version compatibility, Windows behavior or production TLS behavior is established.
The peer runtime log excerpts are summary-only because the attempt-8 remote temporary directory was unavailable when rechecked; no raw peer-log hash is claimed.

The raw pcap SHA-256 and byte length are recorded as producer runtime evidence, but current raw-pcap availability is not independently verified after the attempt-8 temporary directory became unavailable; this entry does not claim raw-pcap-to-sanitized re-derivation.

ambiguousFields.observation: Payload bytes other than prefix positions are sanitized fill bytes.
The protocol-error close is accepted only as a bounded observation and does not establish a maximum accepted production length.

Do not infer any other endian behavior or any field width/order beyond the registered length-prefix width, byte order and payload-length meaning.
Do not infer maximum accepted production length or successful interoperability from the protocol-error close.
